slos.objective: No request ever succeeds in a workspace the actor is not a member of.
99% of interactive runs reach a terminal state without a platform error.
A sandbox is ready to receive work within 10 seconds, 95% of the time.
A step is persisted within 2 seconds of being emitted, 95% of the time.
An API request is answered within 500ms, 95% of the time.
No eval job waits more than 5 minutes before being admitted.

annotations.summary: Somebody was refused access to a workspace they are not a member of.
annotations.runbook: This should never fire. Find the audit_log rows with action='workspace.access_denied' for the window, identify the actor, and establish whether it is a probe, a bug in a client, or a real attempt. The refusal itself worked — this alert is about knowing it happened.

annotations.summary: Sandboxes are taking more than 10s at p95 to become ready.
annotations.runbook: Check the substrate's own status first (Fly machine creation), then whether the image digest changed in the last deploy — a cold image is the usual cause. Runs still work; they start slowly, so this is a page rather than a ticket only because it precedes a queue backup.

annotations.summary: Steps are taking more than 30s to be persisted.
annotations.runbook: The trace is the product; a run whose steps arrive minutes late is a run nobody can watch. Check database write latency and the ingest batch size. At-least-once delivery means nothing is lost while this is firing — it is late, not gone.

annotations.summary: More than 10% of runs are ending in error.
annotations.runbook: Distinguish a provider outage (see jaroku_provider_errors_total by provider) from a platform fault. A provider's bad afternoon is not ours to fix and should be visible on the status page rather than paged on; anything else is.

annotations.summary: A job has been waiting more than 15 minutes.
annotations.runbook: Depth alone does not show this — one workspace's 500-job eval can leave another's single job waiting while the ring rotates. Check the fairness ratio in the load-test report and whether worker replicas are healthy.

annotations.summary: Steps are landing in the DEFAULT partition.
annotations.runbook: Rows there cannot be dropped by month, so the retention promise is quietly not being kept for them. Usually means the partition-ensuring job has not run. Create the missing months and move the rows, in that order.

annotations.summary: A model provider is failing more than one call a second.
annotations.runbook: Check the provider's status page before anything else. Then whether one workspace's key is being rate limited.

annotations.summary: An unusual number of abuse signals in the last hour.
annotations.runbook: Not necessarily abuse: a detector that has started misfiring produces exactly this shape. Check which kind, and whether it is one workspace or many, before touching an enforcement.

annotations.summary: An unusual number of workspaces are under an enforcement rung.
annotations.runbook: The ladder is automatic up to `verify`, so a mis-tuned weight can limit a lot of people at once. Compare against the signal counts; if the signals are flat and the enforcements are not, the thresholds are wrong rather than the customers.

annotations.summary: A lot of requests are being refused by a rate limit.
annotations.runbook: Usually a client with a retry loop. Check whether it is one address or many before changing a limit.
